Source-declared status markers (e.g. 'DESIGNED — NOT IMPLEMENTED') are recorded in v1Justification where relevant.

capabilities.name: Universal identity substrate
capabilities.what: A universal identity system providing seventeen universal identity kinds (persons, organizations, agents, services, devices, systems, etc.) with stable machine-addressable identity for every architectural object.
capabilities.why: Every downstream capability (authorization, tenancy, missions, delegation, evidence) requires stable identity of subjects and objects.
capabilities.v1Justification: Identity is the first loop stage precondition; no request can be authorized or attributed without identity. AGENTS.md §5-6 makes agent identity first-class.

capabilities.name: Authentication surface
capabilities.what: Runtime identity resolution and authentication answering 'Who are you?' before any authorization or execution.
capabilities.why: Authentication is separated from authorization/policy/context by the identity principle; every server function must authenticate first.
capabilities.v1Justification: AGENTS.md §27 server-function rule step 1; mandatory for any production platform.

capabilities.name: Layered authorization model
capabilities.what: Combined RBAC/ABAC/PBAC/ReBAC/RLS/contextual/ownership authorization producing ALLOW/DENY/REDACT/ESCALATE/REQUIRE_APPROVAL decisions from Identity+Tenant+Role+Relationship+Resource+Action+Policy+Context+Risk.
capabilities.why: CoreGrid's layered authorization formula is the universal decision model for every capability and request.
capabilities.v1Justification: No platform can function legitimately without an authorization decision model; explicitly required in server-function rule.

capabilities.name: Domain-neutral universal role taxonomy
capabilities.what: Universal roles (ACTOR, MEMBER, OWNER, ADMINISTRATOR, OPERATOR, MANAGER, SUPERVISOR, CONTRIBUTOR, REVIEWER, APPROVER, AUDITOR, WORKER, AGENT, SERVICE, SYSTEM) independent of any domain vocabulary.
capabilities.why: Roles must not be named after a domain (e.g. no 'Teacher' role in the substrate); domain runtimes map their own role vocabularies onto universal ones.
capabilities.v1Justification: Domain-neutrality is a binding CTO constraint; the universal role layer is required for any domain runtime to exist.

capabilities.name: Agent identity & lifecycle governance
capabilities.what: Every autonomous agent carries Agent ID, Owner, Purpose, Model, Capabilities, Tools, Permissions, Tenant Scope, Memory Scope, Data Scope, Audit Trail, Lifecycle State; lifecycle PROPOSED→REVIEWED→APPROVED→DEPLOYED→MONITORED→SUSPENDED→REVIEWED→RETIRED; no silent permission expansion or self-deployment.
capabilities.why: Agents are untrusted by default and first-class identities; lifecycle governance prevents autonomous authority growth.
capabilities.v1Justification: AI-native platform cannot operate workers/agents without governed identity and lifecycle; direct security invariant.

capabilities.name: Machine-operable Registry
capabilities.what: Machine-addressable registry of architecturally meaningful objects: stable identity, classification, ownership/authority references, provenance, lifecycle registration, version references, relationships, dependencies, capability/contract/state/evidence/conformance references, discoverability, graph traversal, impact-analysis inputs.
capabilities.why: The nervous-system component 01; 'The Registry is a map of CoreGrid's structured architectural reality, not reality itself' — enables impact analysis and discovery for everything else.
capabilities.v1Justification: Machine-operable engineering nervous system is prescribed by the mothers (IMPLEMENTATION.md §12-step chain starts at Registry). Source marker: DESIGNED / NOT CLAIMED — prescribed but not implemented, hence extraction with V1 judgment required at composition.

capabilities.name: Schema system (structural contracts)
capabilities.what: Machine-operable definition, resolution, validation, versioning, composition, evolution, and governance of structural contracts for objects, messages, states, commands, events, artifacts.
capabilities.why: Sits between architectural meaning and machine-operable structure; 'defines structural validity' while not owning meaning, state, evidence, or authority.
capabilities.v1Justification: Typed contracts and Zod-style validation are mandated by AGENTS.md §32; machine nervous system component 02. Source marker: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

capabilities.name: Multi-tenant substrate with mandatory tenant context
capabilities.what: CoreGrid organizes all data and operations under tenants (organizations, schools, campuses, users, devices, twins); every request must carry tenant context; control plane is NOT a tenant.
capabilities.why: Multi-tenancy law: tenant isolation is structural, not optional; every capability must answer WHO/WHICH-TENANT.
capabilities.v1Justification: A domain-neutral multi-tenant production platform requires tenant structuring from day one.

capabilities.name: Tenant isolation (runtime enforcement)
capabilities.what: Runtime tenant isolation: cross-tenant access is structurally impossible; PostgreSQL RLS is mandatory for tenant-sensitive data; application code is never the only security layer.
capabilities.why: Mandatory testing invariant 'Tenant A cannot access Tenant B'; database-level enforcement over application-only checks.
dependsOn: Multi-tenant substrate with mandatory tenant context
capabilities.v1Justification: Security invariant #1 of AGENTS.md §31; non-negotiable for V1.

capabilities.name: Control plane distinct from tenants
capabilities.what: A platform headquarters managing configuration, infrastructure, security, AI operations, billing, compliance, policies, observability, provisioning — structurally separate from tenant surfaces.
capabilities.why: Prevents platform operations from being modeled as a privileged tenant; preserves tenant boundary semantics.
dependsOn: Multi-tenant substrate with mandatory tenant context
capabilities.v1Justification: Platform operations (auth, provisioning, billing, compliance) are required for a legitimate production platform; the 12 mechanisms are 'unified control interfaces, NOT twelve independent microservices'.

capabilities.name: Core reality primitives (25)
capabilities.what: The universal reality vocabulary: entity, state, relationship, event, process, actor, agent, agency, intent, goals, action, intervention, outcome, consequence, causality, causal graph, feedback, emergence, constraints, resources, flows, space, time, conditions, observation (with measurement, evidence, provenance, lineage, uncertainty, confidence, possibility, hypotheses, beliefs, knowledge, decisions, counterfactuals, scenarios, simulation, digital twins, system dynamics, control, adaptation, learning, memory, risk, anomalies following in §6-56).
capabilities.why: Reality-first law: CoreGrid models reality before software; these primitives are the substrate's ontology on which every domain runtime composes.
capabilities.v1Justification: CoreGrid is defined as a Reality Intelligence platform; the primitive set is its constitutive ontology. Sections 148-149 explicitly separate universal from domain semantics, confirming these are universal.

capabilities.name: Universal vs domain semantics separation
capabilities.what: Universal semantics (Entity, State, Event, Process, Relationship, Time, Space, Evidence, Causality) are owned by the substrate; domain semantics (Mining: Mineral Deposit; Education: Student; Agriculture: Field) specialize them; cross-domain reality and domain intersection are supported without embedding domain laws into the universal substrate.
capabilities.why: Domain-neutrality law: 'CoreGrid must support domain laws without embedding every domain's laws into the universal substrate.'
capabilities.v1Justification: The domain-neutral boundary itself must exist in V1 or the platform cannot accept new domains legitimately.

capabilities.name: Domain runtime semantics & registration
capabilities.what: A domain runtime may introduce domain entity types, events, processes, relationships, constraints, causal models, resources, rules, simulations — registered against the substrate; 'CoreGrid is the substrate. Scholar is a runtime. No runtime becomes the dependency root of CoreGrid.'
capabilities.why: Enables education/restaurant/any domain to be instantiated without contaminating the universal ontology.
capabilities.v1Justification: The domain-runtime registration boundary is required for V1 to host its first domain (Scholar) legitimately.

capabilities.name: State system (governed condition representation)
capabilities.what: Representation, tracking, reconstruction, transition, reconciliation, and exposure of current/historical/observed/inferred/intended/planned/predicted/disputed/superseded/unknown condition of subjects with provenance and temporal relationships; fundamental law 'STATE ≠ TRUTH'.
capabilities.why: The V1 loop's Representation/State-Change stages require governed state distinct from truth.
capabilities.v1Justification: State tracking with epistemic distinction is core to the reality loop. Source marker: NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT OPERATIONAL — prescribed.

capabilities.name: Time & space primitives
capabilities.what: Temporal and spatial modeling as first-class reality dimensions (temporal scoping of state, events, evidence).
capabilities.why: Every important claim/state must be temporally scoped (ASSURANCE invariant 38); spatial context needed for physical realities.
capabilities.v1Justification: Temporal scoping is an assurance invariant; without time, states and evidence cannot be reconciled.

capabilities.name: Observation & measurement primitives
capabilities.what: Structured capture of observations and measurements of reality, distinguishable from inference ('Observation ≠ LogEntry' in the reality-to-code mapping).
capabilities.why: The V1 loop begins at Reality → Observation; observation is the entry point of all evidence.
capabilities.v1Justification: The completeness loop explicitly starts with Observation; without structured observation no evidence exists.

capabilities.name: Evidence fabric (7 classes + provenance + integrity)
capabilities.what: Machine-operable evidence infrastructure: 7 evidence classes (direct, derived, reported, generated, reconstructed, simulated, predicted — 'Simulation and prediction must never silently become direct observation'), 21-field provenance, lineage, integrity protection against tampering; evidence does not determine ultimate truth.
capabilities.why: Evidence is the substrate of claims, verification, conformance, and progress; the V1 loop's Evidence stage.
capabilities.v1Justification: 'No evidence, no verified completion' (PROGRESS.md §17); evidence fabric is mandatory for the loop to close.

capabilities.name: Evidence lifecycle (sufficiency, confidence, revocation, retention, chain)
capabilities.what: Evidence sufficiency assessment, confidence scoring, revocation (revoked evidence cannot silently support active claims), retention policy, and evidence chaining.
capabilities.why: Evidence must be governed over time, not just captured; stale/revoked evidence must be detectable.
capabilities.v1Justification: Revocation and staleness invariants (ASSURANCE invariants 12-13) are mandatory correctness invariants for any platform claiming verified state.

capabilities.name: Claim architecture
capabilities.what: Claims as first-class assertions with claimant, scope, target, time, basis, evidence, assessment, uncertainty, status; claim states PROPOSED/SUPPORTED/CONDITIONALLY_SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED/DISPUTED/STALE/REVOKED/SUPERSEDED/UNKNOWN; claim graph.
capabilities.why: 'A claim is not permanently true merely because it was once supported' — claims mediate between evidence and verification.
capabilities.v1Justification: Separating claims from truth is a canonical-truth invariant (AGENTS.md §9); required for trustworthy reporting.

capabilities.name: Thirteen epistemic truth states
capabilities.what: A 13-state epistemic vocabulary distinguishing verified, supported, disputed, unknown, stale, etc., for every modeled fact; 'Unknown must remain unknown', 'Stale must remain distinguishable from current' (RUNTIME invariants 25-26).
capabilities.why: Reality knowledge cannot be boolean; the truth-state model is the canonical-truth backbone.
capabilities.v1Justification: Distinguishing unknown from false is a loop integrity requirement; without it memory and progress corrupt.

capabilities.name: Causality & causal graph
capabilities.what: Explicit causality modeling and causal graphs, distinct from correlation ('CAUSATION AND CORRELATION' RUNTIME §45; IMPLEMENTATION correlation-vs-causation rule).
capabilities.why: Intelligence and outcome reasoning require causal structure, not merely co-occurrence.
capabilities.v1Justification: Outcome/verification reasoning in the loop depends on causal claims; prescribed as universal ontology.

capabilities.name: Hypotheses, beliefs, knowledge & conflicting knowledge
capabilities.what: Derived epistemic objects (hypotheses, beliefs, knowledge) with explicit conflict handling between competing knowledge items and knowledge evolution over time.
capabilities.why: Intelligence must distinguish derived understanding (AGENTS.md §9 Intelligence) from reality and handle contradictions explicitly.
capabilities.v1Justification: Conflict handling is required the moment two evidence-bearing claims disagree; canonical-truth principle demands it.

capabilities.name: Decisions as reality objects
capabilities.what: Decisions modeled as first-class reality objects with authority, context, rationale, and outcome linkage.
capabilities.why: The V1 loop's Decision stage must be observable and auditable, not implicit in code paths.
capabilities.v1Justification: Decision is an explicit loop stage; auditability requires decision objects.

capabilities.name: Counterfactuals, scenarios & simulation
capabilities.what: Counterfactual worlds, possible futures, scenario and simulation modeling with intervention→counterfactual linkage; simulation is distinct from observation.
capabilities.why: Reality Intelligence capability: what-if reasoning without mutating canonical truth.
capabilities.v1Justification: Prescribed as core reality ontology, but simulation infra is heavyweight; source gives no V1 execution marker for simulation runtime. Extracted as unknown pending CTO composition.

capabilities.name: Digital Twin substrate
capabilities.what: Authorized digital models of reality carrying identity, owner, tenant, relationships, state, history, events, capabilities, permissions, policies, memory, observations, predictions, audit rules; 'A Digital Twin is not a permission bypass.'
capabilities.why: Twins are the representation stage for physical/institutional realities.
dependsOn: Multi-tenant substrate with mandatory tenant context
capabilities.v1Justification: Twin governance requirements are prescribed, but the corpus does not mark twins as V1-minimum; twins depend on the full state/observation stack. Source: phase-16 Digital Twin registered as a later phase in DECISIONS.md phase scope.

capabilities.name: Universal memory primitive
capabilities.what: Memory as a reality primitive: retention of observations, knowledge, and history enabling learning and recall; knowledge evolution over time.
capabilities.why: The V1 loop closes at Memory → Observation; without memory the loop cannot iterate.
capabilities.v1Justification: Memory is the loop's consolidation stage; mandated by the CTO loop definition.

capabilities.name: Worker memory scoping
capabilities.what: Worker memory is scoped (session/mission/long-term) with explicit memory-scope identity fields; no silent memory expansion.
capabilities.why: Prevents agents from accumulating unauthorized context across missions/tenants.
capabilities.v1Justification: Memory-scope is part of the binding agent identity model; expansion requires review (AGENTS.md §8).

capabilities.name: Risk & anomaly primitives
capabilities.what: Risk modeling and anomaly detection as reality-level constructs feeding decisions and interventions.
capabilities.why: Risk controls are part of the authorization decision; anomalies trigger observation→action loops.
capabilities.v1Justification: Risk is an input to every authorization decision (AGENTS.md §16 formula); minimal risk surfacing is V1-required.

capabilities.name: Partial observability, missingness & reality reconciliation
capabilities.what: Explicit handling of incomplete observation (missingness, partial observability) and reconciliation of divergent reality representations into consistent truth states.
capabilities.why: Real platforms never observe everything; unknown must be represented, never guessed.
capabilities.v1Justification: Reconciliation is required to keep state, evidence, and reality from silently diverging.

capabilities.name: Context sovereignty law
capabilities.what: Accessible ≠ Relevant ≠ Authorized ≠ Safe; context does not grant permission; mission context derived only from authoritative sources; context packages are bounded and provenance-preserving.
capabilities.why: Prevents context assembly from becoming an authorization bypass — the classic AI-platform failure.
capabilities.v1Justification: Security invariant for any AI-native platform; explicitly a runtime law and mission law.

capabilities.name: Context Assembly System
capabilities.what: Transformation of distributed authoritative information into a bounded, provenance-preserving, mission-specific Context Package: relevance, authority/access, temporal, dependency, conflict/consistency filtering; determines sufficiency and records exclusions and uncertainty.
capabilities.why: Every worker/mission/decision consumes assembled context; unbounded context is both a security and correctness hazard.
capabilities.v1Justification: Context is an explicit loop stage; workers cannot receive authorized bounded context without an assembly mechanism. Source marker: NOT ESTABLISHED.

capabilities.name: Canonical intelligence abstraction (capability→model role→provider adapter)
capabilities.what: INTELLIGENCE REQUIREMENT → CAPABILITY → MODEL ROLE → PROVIDER ADAPTER → MODEL; missions state required intelligence capability, never 'Use Model X'; provider neutrality preserved; centralized AI gateway for routing/auth/cost/safety/logging/fallback.
capabilities.why: Prevents provider-specific implementation from becoming architectural authority; enables model substitution.
capabilities.v1Justification: The AI-native platform's core abstraction; AGENTS.md §20 mandates gateway centralization in V1.

capabilities.name: Capability registry (worker & intelligence)
capabilities.what: Registries of intelligence capabilities (long_context_reasoning, code_generation, classification, structured_extraction, planning, security_analysis, domain_reasoning, visual_reasoning...) and worker capabilities (20 specialist capabilities, capability matrix) used for capability matching rather than model/agent-name selection.
capabilities.why: Capability-over-agent-count principle: work is assigned to capabilities, not to named agents or models.
capabilities.v1Justification: Capability matching is the delegation contract's prerequisite; prescribed across RUNTIME/WORKFORCE/CP-07.

capabilities.name: AI privacy & minimization pipeline
capabilities.what: Before data reaches a model: identity → authorization → classification → purpose check → minimization → redaction → AI context → model.
capabilities.why: AI receives only authorized, minimized information; classification and purpose are enforced pre-inference.
capabilities.v1Justification: Privacy law; tenant-sensitive platform cannot send unauthorized data to models.

capabilities.name: AI output trust & proposal pipeline
capabilities.what: AI output is untrusted by default: AI Proposal → Validation → Policy Check → Approval → Execution → Audit; no model output becomes assurance/architecture merely because a model generated it; AI interpretation distinguishable from authoritative decisions.
capabilities.why: AI sovereignty boundary: AI may propose, humans/systems approve; critical actions require the full pipeline.
capabilities.v1Justification: Self-improvement law (AGENTS.md §8) requires this for any AI-assisted engineering in V1.

capabilities.name: Multimodal intelligence support
capabilities.what: Multimodal analysis listed as an intelligence requirement class alongside text reasoning capabilities.
capabilities.why: Intelligence requirements are capability-typed; multimodal is one capability class.
capabilities.v1Justification: Prescribed as a capability class but not marked as a V1-minimum requirement anywhere in the corpus.

capabilities.name: Runtime event model
capabilities.what: Structured runtime events as first-class records (Event ≠ LogEntry in the reality-to-code mapping); ecosystem events; events feed evidence and state.
capabilities.why: Events are the observable currency of execution and reality change.
capabilities.v1Justification: State changes must be observable; events are the mechanism.

capabilities.name: Command & query models
capabilities.what: Typed command model (intents that mutate state under authority) and query model (reads under authorization), separated from events.
capabilities.why: Command/query/event separation is required for idempotency, auditability, and authorization of writes vs reads.
capabilities.v1Justification: Server-function rule requires validated, authorized, audited mutations; command contracts are the mechanism.

capabilities.name: Mission model (15-element law, types, lifecycle, states)
capabilities.what: Missions as the unit of governed work: 15-element mission law, 12 constitutional laws, 22-component canonical mission model, 19 mission types, 17-stage lifecycle, 19 mission states.
capabilities.why: Missions transform intent into bounded, observable, closable work — the Mission/Delegation/Worker-Execution stages of the loop.
capabilities.v1Justification: Mission orchestration is the loop's control spine; prescribed by IMPLEMENTATION.md 12-step chain.

capabilities.name: Mission gates (13 categories, 8 states)
capabilities.what: Explicit control points preventing premature progression: Definition, Architecture, Contract, Security, Planning, Workforce, Execution, Verification, Integration, Validation, Conformance, Evidence, Closure gates; states NOT_STARTED/READY/PASSED/PASSED_WITH_CONDITIONS/BLOCKED/FAILED/WAIVED/NOT_APPLICABLE.
capabilities.why: Gates enforce loop ordering — verification cannot be skipped; evidence gate cannot be waived silently.
dependsOn: Mission model (15-element law, types, lifecycle, states)
capabilities.v1Justification: Gate discipline is the enforcement mechanism of 'no evidence, no completion'.

capabilities.name: Mission failure, recovery, handoff, closure, reopening, history
capabilities.what: Failure remains traceable; recovery does not erase history; handoffs preserve context and accountability; closure does not erase execution history; reopening does not rewrite previous closure; mission history remains auditable.
capabilities.why: History immutability laws protect auditability across the entire mission lifecycle.
dependsOn: Mission model (15-element law, types, lifecycle, states)
capabilities.v1Justification: AGENTS.md §28 immutable audit records; mission laws 15-18, 25.

capabilities.name: Mission Orchestration System
capabilities.what: Machine-operable transformation of an approved mission into a controlled lifecycle: decomposition, dependency resolution, work-unit formation, context/workforce requirements, delegation requests, authorized execution, result collection, verification, integration, conformance, evidence, reconciliation, closure.
capabilities.why: The bridge between approved intent and executable work preserving authority, scope, evidence, and human authority.
dependsOn: Mission model (15-element law, types, lifecycle, states)
capabilities.v1Justification: Loop stages Mission→Delegation→Worker Execution require an orchestrator. Source marker: NOT ESTABLISHED.

capabilities.name: Capability-over-agent-count & dynamic workforce principle
capabilities.what: Workforce is measured by capability coverage, not agent count; 'Agent ⊂ Workforce'; dynamic assembly: mission requirements → capability extraction → risk analysis → worker selection → context assembly → permission assignment → worker instantiation → execution.
capabilities.why: Workers are instantiated per mission; no permanent worker army; capability coverage formula governs sufficiency.
capabilities.v1Justification: Worker Execution is a loop stage; dynamic instantiation is how the AI-native platform does work.

capabilities.name: Worker instance model
capabilities.what: Model + Role + Context + Permissions + Mission + Tools = Worker Instance; 7 worker types; 20 specialist capabilities + capability matrix; model-role neutrality ('Architecture Reviewer' not 'Claude Architecture Reviewer'); tool roles with authority/isolation/provenance.
capabilities.why: Workers are composable, substitutable, model-neutral units — no model owns authority.
capabilities.v1Justification: Worker Execution loop stage requires a defined worker unit; model neutrality is a CTO binding constraint.

capabilities.name: Bounded delegation & delegation chain
capabilities.what: Delegation does not transfer ultimate authority; delegation chains are bounded; a worker cannot manufacture mission authority; a model cannot become architectural authority through capability.
capabilities.why: Authority non-transfer is a runtime and mission law; delegation must be traceable and bounded.
capabilities.v1Justification: Security invariant; prevents delegation-based privilege escalation.

capabilities.name: Workforce Delegation mechanism
capabilities.what: Controlled capability matching: mission requirements → work requirements → required capabilities → eligibility → authorized workforce options → capability/constraint matching → delegation decision → delegation contract → worker provisioning → execution → verification → release/reassign/escalate.
capabilities.why: 'It does not merely assign agents' — the controlled bridge between mission orchestration and execution.
capabilities.v1Justification: Delegation is an explicit loop stage. Source marker: NOT ESTABLISHED.

capabilities.name: Worker collaboration, parallelization, handoffs, reviews, escalation, conflict resolution
capabilities.what: Parallel-safe work, collaboration protocols, handoff contracts, independent review of worker output, escalation paths, and structured conflict resolution between workers.
capabilities.why: Multi-worker missions require coordination primitives with verification and conflict surfacing.
capabilities.v1Justification: Completeness test requires collaboration, parallel safety, handoffs, independent verification, escalation, replacement — all as functioning capability coverage.

capabilities.name: Worker lifecycle & replacement
capabilities.what: Worker provisioning, monitoring, suspension, replacement of failed workers, workforce failure management.
capabilities.why: Failed workers must be replaceable without losing mission state (replaceability is an engineering law).
capabilities.v1Justification: ENGINEERING.md failure-first law; missions must survive worker failure.

capabilities.name: Worker permissions & security
capabilities.what: Bounded permission assignment per worker; least privilege; worker security including tool isolation and exfiltration controls.
capabilities.why: Permissions cannot silently expand (RUNTIME invariant 22); workers are untrusted by default.
capabilities.v1Justification: Mandatory testing invariant 'Agent cannot exceed permissions'.

capabilities.name: Workforce verification
capabilities.what: Independent verification of worker output; worker completion is not verification; an AI worker must not validate its own unsupported claim.
capabilities.why: Separates execution from acceptance — the loop's Verification stage.
capabilities.v1Justification: Verification independence is a mandatory invariant in three mothers; V1 loop requires it.

capabilities.name: Workforce economics
capabilities.what: Economic accounting of workforce consumption (compute, model usage, tool usage) attributable to missions and tenants.
capabilities.why: Cost tracking is part of the AI gateway mandate; economic attribution supports billing and governance.
capabilities.v1Justification: AGENTS.md §20 requires cost tracking in the AI gateway; economic attribution is required for institutional operation.

capabilities.name: Human–AI collaboration model
capabilities.what: Defined collaboration modes between human and AI workers, including human verification authority and approval obligations.
capabilities.why: AI sovereignty boundary requires human governance over AI proposals; escalations terminate in human authority.
dependsOn: Worker collaboration, parallelization, handoffs, reviews, escalation, conflict resolution
capabilities.v1Justification: Approval steps in the AI trust pipeline are human or authorized-system obligations; required for V1 legitimacy.

capabilities.name: Cursor workforce boundary
capabilities.what: Engineering-tool execution surfaces (e.g. Cursor) are a workforce boundary, not CoreGrid runtime authority: 'Cursor execution is an engineering-tool boundary, not a CoreGrid runtime authority.'
capabilities.why: Prevents development tools from being conflated with platform runtime authority.
capabilities.v1Justification: Authority hygiene: tool boundary must be explicit from V1 to avoid hidden autonomy.

capabilities.name: Workforce machine registry
capabilities.what: Machine-readable registry of workforce definitions (worker types, capability declarations, model roles, tool bindings, runtime profiles).
capabilities.why: Workforce assembly and delegation must be machine-operable, not prose.
capabilities.v1Justification: Delegation contracts require machine-readable workforce definitions.

capabilities.name: Execution System (bounded runtime execution)
capabilities.what: Transformation of an authorized delegation and executable contract into controlled runtime actions and observable outcomes: MISSION → WORK UNIT → DELEGATION → AUTHORIZED EXECUTION CONTRACT → EXECUTION PLAN/COMMAND → EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT → ACTION → RUNTIME EFFECT → OBSERVATION → EXECUTION EVIDENCE → VERIFICATION.
capabilities.why: 'Its responsibility is to safely execute what has already been authorized' — the loop's Action/State-Change stages.
capabilities.v1Justification: Worker Execution loop stage. Source marker: NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT OBSERVED.

capabilities.name: Bounded execution formula & runtime laws
capabilities.what: Execution only within bounded authority: every authorization bounded, every meaningful execution attributable, no silent side effects, no hidden autonomy, autonomy cannot self-expand, high-impact actions require stronger controls.
capabilities.why: The 9 runtime laws define safe execution semantics for all machine action.
capabilities.v1Justification: Security invariants; 'Every authorization must be bounded' and 'Every meaningful execution must be attributable' are runtime invariants 36-37.

capabilities.name: Execution lifecycle controls (cancellation, timeouts, retry, idempotency, checkpoints, rollback, recovery, quarantine, escalation)
capabilities.what: Full execution lifecycle semantics: cancellation, timeout enforcement, bounded retry, idempotency, checkpoints, rollback, recovery, quarantine of suspicious execution, escalation paths.
capabilities.why: Failure is a first-class runtime condition; recovery must be observable (RUNTIME invariant 29).
capabilities.v1Justification: Production platform requires failure semantics; failure tests are mandated by AGENTS.md §31.

capabilities.name: Resource runtime (leases, concurrency)
capabilities.what: Resource classes, lease-based resource allocation, concurrency control over shared resources and execution.
capabilities.why: Parallel workers and missions contend for resources; uncontrolled concurrency corrupts state.
dependsOn: Execution lifecycle controls (cancellation, timeouts, retry, idempotency, checkpoints, rollback, recovery, quarantine, escalation)
capabilities.v1Justification: Concurrency/idempotency rules exist in IMPLEMENTATION.md; required for correct multi-worker execution.

capabilities.name: Tool runtime & sandbox architecture
capabilities.what: Tool execution surfaces with isolation (sandbox architecture), tool boundary law (tools execute, they do not authorize), tool provenance.
capabilities.why: Tools are untrusted execution surfaces; isolation prevents tool compromise from becoming system compromise.
capabilities.v1Justification: Tool boundary law is a runtime law; supply-chain and artifact defense depend on it.

capabilities.name: External system boundary
capabilities.what: External systems are never automatically trusted; integration goes through adapters with explicit trust decisions, failure semantics, and contracts.
capabilities.why: Provider-agnostic architecture; external failures must be contained.
capabilities.v1Justification: Integration failure handling is prescribed (IMPLEMENTATION.md §76); provider neutrality is an invariant.

capabilities.name: Security & trust runtime (identity, capability security, least privilege, domain/environment isolation, secrets)
capabilities.what: Runtime identity, authentication, authorization, capability security, least privilege, tenant isolation, domain isolation, environment isolation, and secret security as runtime architecture — 'Security is part of runtime architecture' (invariant 34).
capabilities.why: Security fabric is continuous: observe → evaluate → policy check → decide → enforce → audit.
dependsOn: Multi-tenant substrate with mandatory tenant context
capabilities.v1Justification: Mandatory security invariants (AGENTS.md §31); secrets law §30.

capabilities.name: AI-specific runtime defenses (prompt injection, malicious artifacts, exfiltration, supply chain)
capabilities.what: Prompt-injection defense, malicious-artifact defense, exfiltration control, and supply-chain security as first-class runtime capabilities.
capabilities.why: AI-native platforms face AI-specific threat classes; these defenses are prescribed runtime architecture, not add-ons.
dependsOn: Security & trust runtime (identity, capability security, least privilege, domain/environment isolation, secrets)
capabilities.v1Justification: Security tests for AI threats are mandated by ENGINEERING.md AI security threat model; an AI-native platform is not production-legitimate without them.

capabilities.name: Verification architecture
capabilities.what: Requirement + expected result + observed execution/evidence → verification finding + evidence assessment + verification state + provenance; verification plan/procedure/run/results/findings; verification states (6 states in ENGINEERING.md); 'It does not automatically declare production readiness'.
capabilities.why: The loop's Verification stage; transforms observation into justified conclusions.
capabilities.v1Justification: 'No evidence, no verified completion'; verification is a mandatory loop stage. Source marker: NOT IMPLEMENTED.

capabilities.name: Verification vs validation separation
capabilities.what: Verification (did we build it right per requirements) is distinct from validation (does it behave correctly in intended context); both are distinct mission gates.
capabilities.why: Conflating them hides context-of-use failures.
capabilities.v1Justification: Mission law 12 and separate Integration/Validation gates require it.

capabilities.name: Human verification & adversarial verification
capabilities.what: Human verification authority for critical claims; adversarial verification (attempting to disprove claims) as a verification mode; 'Assurance must remain capable of disproving CoreGrid's own assumptions' (self-questioning law §153).
capabilities.why: Independent and adversarial checks prevent systemic self-confirmation bias.
capabilities.v1Justification: Verification independence invariant (26: critical assurance independently evaluated); AI workers cannot self-validate.

capabilities.name: Reproducibility & uncertainty handling
capabilities.what: Verification results must be reproducible; uncertainty is first-class — inconclusive must not silently become PASS; unknown is not false.
capabilities.why: Epistemic honesty invariants: PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE/UNKNOWN states must be preserved.
capabilities.v1Justification: Inconclusive≠pass is assurance invariant 11; reproducibility is an engineering law.

capabilities.name: Conformance System
capabilities.what: Machine-operable comparison DECLARED → IMPLEMENTED → OBSERVED: does the implementation/runtime conform to declared authority, architecture, contracts, policies within scope and version; conformance states; 'Verification is not conformance' and conformance is not architectural authority.
capabilities.why: Detects divergence between what CoreGrid declared and what it actually is.
capabilities.v1Justification: Progress measured by 'verified capability and conformance' (PROGRESS.md §00) — conformance is required for truthful progress. Source marker: DESIGNED — NOT IMPLEMENTED.

capabilities.name: Progress Reconciliation
capabilities.what: Truthful engineering progress reconciled from mission intent, declared requirements, implementation state, execution observations, verification/conformance results, evidence, runtime observations, gaps, dependencies, drift, and time; 23 progress dimensions; progress object model; 'no single percentage law'; progress may regress.
capabilities.why: 'Progress is not activity' — prevents volume-based progress claims.
capabilities.v1Justification: PROGRESS.md §00 progress law is binding on any V1 build reporting; reconciliation is how V1 reports truthfully. Source marker: NOT OPERATIONAL.

capabilities.name: Drift & Evolution System
capabilities.what: Continuous reconciliation of differences across governance, architecture, reality model, phases, missions, contracts, schemas, registries, state, evidence, implementation, configuration, deployment, runtime, docs, models, policies, dependencies, external systems; distinguishes DRIFT / INTENTIONAL CHANGE / UNKNOWN DIFFERENCE / EXPECTED VARIATION; controls authorized evolution with baselines.
capabilities.why: The loop's evolution boundary: 'Drift detection is not evolution authority; evolution proposal is not evolution approval; every evolution must establish a new baseline.'
capabilities.v1Justification: Architecture evolves in V1; unauthorized drift must be detectable from day one. Source marker: NOT OPERATIONAL.

capabilities.name: Baseline architecture
capabilities.what: Versioned architectural baselines; historical baselines remain reconstructable; new baselines preserve history.
capabilities.why: Drift comparison requires a baseline; reconstruction requires preserved history.
capabilities.v1Justification: Invariants 24-25 (baseline establishment and reconstructability).

capabilities.name: Governance hierarchy & authority levels
capabilities.what: Layered authority: constitution → governance → architecture → domain mothers → phase/mission/blueprint → implementation; conflicts resolve by precedence (security invariants > privacy > constitution > ADRs > phases > schema > RLS > API > domain > implementation > tests > docs).
capabilities.why: Every capability must answer 'under which policy'; conflict resolution requires a total order of authority.
capabilities.v1Justification: Binding: AGENTS.md §4 encodes the precedence; V1 cannot resolve contradictions without it. NOTE: the corpus itself disagrees on the exact ladder (see contradictions).

capabilities.name: Canonical mother-surface authorship model
capabilities.what: Canonical knowledge lives in designated mother surfaces; governance discourages permanent derivative governance documents; second-generation mothers (IMPLEMENTATION, RUNTIME, ASSURANCE) self-declare a three-mother engineering triad.
capabilities.why: Prevents authority fragmentation across unowned documents.
capabilities.v1Justification: V1 reconstruction needs a defined canonical-surface set; the count itself is contradicted in the corpus (see contradictions).

capabilities.name: Architecture decision records
capabilities.what: Persistent records of architectural decisions (AD-001..AD-067) binding future implementation; decisions scoped to registered phases.
capabilities.why: Change management requires ADRs; decisions are authoritative rationale, not suggestions.
capabilities.v1Justification: AGENTS.md §38 requires ADRs for large changes; V1 evolution must produce and respect decision records.

capabilities.name: Boundary & ownership model (one capability one owner)
capabilities.what: One canonical capability or authoritative state → one explicit owner → explicit boundary → governed contract → controlled authority; ownership matrices; duplicate-authority detection; circular dependency analysis.
capabilities.why: Ownership ambiguity is the root of governance failure; duplicate authority must be detectable.
capabilities.v1Justification: IMPLEMENTATION.md duplicate-authority detection is part of the prescribed build chain; V1 must not ship unowned capabilities.

capabilities.name: Dependency topology governance
capabilities.what: Canonical dependency topology over phases, capabilities, runtimes, actors, agents, domains, data, knowledge, memory, policies, contracts, events, commands, infrastructure; 7-layer dependency hierarchy; 'No runtime becomes the dependency root of CoreGrid'.
capabilities.why: Prevents dependency inversion (runtime becoming root), circular dependencies, and ownership violations.
dependsOn: Boundary & ownership model (one capability one owner)
capabilities.v1Justification: Domain logic must not depend on vendors (AGENTS.md §24); dependency law is structural, not advisory.

capabilities.name: Registry meta-law (canonical architectural index)
capabilities.what: The registry as structural memory: CONSTITUTION → LAWS → LAYERS → PHASES → CAPABILITIES → CONTRACTS → SERVICES → IMPLEMENTATIONS → RUNTIME INSTANCES → OBSERVED SYSTEM; continuously answers what exists, why, where it belongs.
capabilities.why: The machine-readable index binds declared architecture to implementable structure.
capabilities.v1Justification: IMPLEMENTATION.md 12-step chain begins with Registry; V1 needs a canonical index to reconstruct from. NOTE: REGISTRY.md self-declares v4.0/CANONICAL — generation conflict recorded.

capabilities.name: Blueprint pipeline (charter → parsing → decomposition → extraction)
capabilities.what: Blueprint authority principle ('a blueprint is not automatically architecture'), 16-granularity blueprint unit, 8 authority classifications, 5-dimension classification + Blueprint Intelligence Graph, 14-stage parsing pipeline, decomposition, capability extraction distinguishing capability/implementation/mechanism/requirement/outcome, capability normalization/dedup ('UNMAPPED is a finding').
capabilities.why: Turns external/legacy architecture text into governed, deduplicated capability inventories with preserved provenance.
capabilities.v1Justification: This V1 reconstruction itself is a blueprint-pipeline exercise; the mechanism is prescribed for ingesting any future architecture corpus.

capabilities.name: Blueprint dependency mapping & architecture gap detection
capabilities.what: Dependency analysis from blueprints (analyzed, not copied) and explicit architecture-gap findings ('Architecture gaps must become explicit findings').
capabilities.why: Gaps between declared and required architecture must be surfaced, never silently absorbed.
capabilities.v1Justification: Gap detection is required for honest V1 completeness claims.

capabilities.name: Blueprint contract/security/runtime/implementation extraction
capabilities.what: Extraction of contracts, security requirements, runtime requirements, and implementation requirements from blueprints; security requirements must survive decomposition; runtime requirements must not disappear into implementation details.
capabilities.why: Decomposition must not drop security/runtime obligations.
capabilities.v1Justification: Blueprint laws 18-19 make security/runtime survival mandatory during decomposition.

capabilities.name: Blueprint conflict detection, reconciliation, versioning, supersession
capabilities.what: Conflict detection between blueprints, reconciliation preserving original claims, versioning keeping versions distinguishable, supersession keeping superseded blueprints traceable.
capabilities.why: Blueprint corpus evolves; contradictions must be preserved, not overwritten.
capabilities.v1Justification: This reconstruction contradicts-and-reconciles the corpus; the mechanism is the prescribed way to do it.

capabilities.name: Blueprint-to-mission translation
capabilities.what: Translation of blueprints into missions with preserved lineage; one blueprint may produce many missions; many blueprints may contribute to one mission.
capabilities.why: Links declared architecture to governed execution.
dependsOn: Mission model (15-element law, types, lifecycle, states)
capabilities.v1Justification: Lineage preservation law 23; missions without provenance break auditability.

capabilities.name: Engineering constitution & laws
capabilities.what: Engineering laws: failure-first, replaceability, reproducibility, traceability, plus repository archaeology and context sovereignty for engineering work.
capabilities.why: Engineering behavior is governed, not ad hoc; failure is designed for, not discovered.
capabilities.v1Justification: V1 is built by governed engineering; these laws bind the build itself.

capabilities.name: Architecture-to-code mapping rules
capabilities.what: Entity≠Record, State≠FieldValue, Event≠LogEntry, Observation≠LogLine — canonical architectural concepts must not be collapsed into storage/implementation artifacts.
capabilities.why: Prevents implementation artifacts from silently becoming the ontology.
capabilities.v1Justification: Canonical truth principle (AGENTS.md §9) requires the distinction to survive implementation.

capabilities.name: Contracts system (17 categories, typed contracts)
capabilities.what: 17 contract categories; object/command/query/event/error contracts with required fields; typed contracts with validation.
capabilities.why: Every cross-boundary interaction is contract-governed.
capabilities.v1Justification: API governance (AGENTS.md §26) requires validated contracts; Zod/typed contracts mandated by AGENTS.md §32.

capabilities.name: Implementation rules (idempotency, state integrity, side effects)
capabilities.what: Idempotent operations, state integrity enforcement, explicit side-effect management and attribution.
capabilities.why: Distributed, retrying, multi-worker systems corrupt state without these rules.
dependsOn: Execution lifecycle controls (cancellation, timeouts, retry, idempotency, checkpoints, rollback, recovery, quarantine, escalation)
capabilities.v1Justification: Required for loop integrity (Action → State Change → Evidence).

capabilities.name: Testing spectrum (13 levels, negative testing)
capabilities.what: 13-level testing spectrum including negative testing and failure tests; mandatory invariants: tenant A cannot access tenant B, user A cannot access user B, agent cannot exceed permissions, expired access fails, revoked access fails.
capabilities.why: Testing standard is mandatory for every major feature.
capabilities.v1Justification: AGENTS.md §31 mandatory invariants are binding for V1.

capabilities.name: Runtime conformance (engineering)
capabilities.what: Establishment of runtime conformance to declared architecture during engineering, feeding the conformance system.
capabilities.why: Bridges engineering-time verification and runtime conformance.
capabilities.v1Justification: Progress dimension 22 'runtime conformance' is part of the 23-dimension progress model.

capabilities.name: Quality gates (engineering)
capabilities.what: Engineering quality gates preventing progression without satisfied quality conditions.
capabilities.why: Mission gates need engineering-time counterparts.
capabilities.v1Justification: Gate discipline is required for verified completion claims.

capabilities.name: Engineering debt, drift, change management
capabilities.what: Explicit debt registers, engineering drift detection, and governed change management with rollback planning.
capabilities.why: Debt and drift must be tracked artifacts, not folklore.
capabilities.v1Justification: Completeness test questions 16-17 (what debt remains, what drift could occur).

capabilities.name: AI-assisted engineering governance
capabilities.what: Governance of AI participation in engineering: AI security threat model, AI observability metadata, AI proposals vs human authority, self-improvement ≠ permission expansion.
capabilities.why: CoreGrid's engineering is AI-assisted by design; un-governed AI engineering is an untrusted supply chain.
capabilities.v1Justification: The platform builds itself with AI workers from V1; governance of that is not deferrable.

capabilities.name: Engineering workflow & state model
capabilities.what: Defined engineering workflow and engineering state model (engineering work has states, not just completion).
capabilities.why: Engineering progress must be stateful and observable.
capabilities.v1Justification: Feeds progress reconciliation inputs.

capabilities.name: Engineering completeness model & test
capabilities.what: 17-question completeness test: what capability does this implement, what reality does it represent, who owns it, what contracts govern it, dependencies, reverse dependencies, failure behavior, security, observation, testing, verification, deployment, recovery, runtime conformance, evidence, debt, drift.
capabilities.why: Definition of Done is operationalized as a checklist binding architecture+implementation+security+tests+docs+observability+operations.
capabilities.v1Justification: AGENTS.md §41 definition of done requires exactly this operationalization.

capabilities.name: Physical architecture (modules, service extraction criteria, API architecture)
capabilities.what: Physical module categories, service-extraction criteria, API architecture, synchronous vs asynchronous boundaries, transaction boundaries.
capabilities.why: Implementation architecture must follow declared criteria, not ad hoc decomposition.
capabilities.v1Justification: A production platform needs a defined physical strategy; monolith-first with extraction criteria is the prescribed initial strategy.

capabilities.name: Persistence & data architecture (data categories, primary database role, object storage, audit persistence, retention, backup)
capabilities.what: Data categories, primary database role, object storage, repository/filesystem role, secrets storage, data consistency, state/evidence/audit persistence, retention, backup and recovery.
capabilities.why: Database law: constraints, indexes, transactions, foreign keys, RLS, migrations, immutable audit records.
capabilities.v1Justification: AGENTS.md §28 database law is binding; audit immutability is a security invariant.

capabilities.name: Repository architecture (mother surfaces, machine-operable directories)
capabilities.what: Top-level mother surfaces and machine-operable directory structure (registry/, state/, evidence/, temporary/) binding canonical, structured, runtime, evidence, and temporary separation.
capabilities.why: Canonical/structured/runtime separation is enforced physically in the repository (see ECOSYSTEM.md §53 pattern).
capabilities.v1Justification: V1 reconstruction writes into this exact structure; the separation is prescribed.

capabilities.name: Engineering bootstrap (stages, dependency law, phase states)
capabilities.what: Bootstrap principle, ordered bootstrap stages, bootstrap dependency law, implementation phase states.
capabilities.why: The platform must be able to build itself from nothing in a governed order.
capabilities.v1Justification: V1 IS the bootstrap; its stages are prescribed.

capabilities.name: Integration architecture (internal, external, failure)
capabilities.what: Internal integration rules, external integration via adapters, integration failure semantics.
capabilities.why: Provider-agnostic integration with explicit failure behavior.
capabilities.v1Justification: Provider neutrality (AGENTS.md §25) requires adapter-based integration in V1.

capabilities.name: Version & migration architecture
capabilities.what: Version principle, migration rules, historical compatibility guarantees.
capabilities.why: Schema/state evolution without breaking history (invariant 40: new baselines preserve history).
dependsOn: Persistence & data architecture (data categories, primary database role, object storage, audit persistence, retention, backup)
capabilities.v1Justification: Migrations law in AGENTS.md §28; historical reconstructability invariant.

capabilities.name: Implementation security boundaries (trust zones, least privilege)
capabilities.what: Trust zones and least-privilege boundaries in the physical implementation.
capabilities.why: Physical deployment must encode the logical security model.
dependsOn: Security & trust runtime (identity, capability security, least privilege, domain/environment isolation, secrets)
capabilities.v1Justification: Zero-trust boundaries are prescribed in control-plane law; physical enforcement is mandatory.

capabilities.name: Observability requirements
capabilities.what: Logs, metrics, traces, events, audits, health checks for everything important; AI observability metadata; never log passwords/tokens/secrets/unnecessary private data.
capabilities.why: Assurance observability and auditability (§133-134) require the telemetry substrate.
capabilities.v1Justification: 'Assurance itself must be observable' (invariant 27); required in V1.

capabilities.name: Reliability engineering (SLO/SLI)
capabilities.what: Service level objectives and indicators for important services; reliability assurance (availability, capacity, backup/restoration).
capabilities.why: Institutional platform operations require defined reliability targets.
capabilities.v1Justification: Production-readiness dimension 21 in the progress model requires reliability validation.

capabilities.name: Failure architecture (taxonomy, response, detection, classification, containment, incidents, recovery)
capabilities.what: Failure taxonomy, response model, detection, classification, containment, incident architecture, recovery architecture; security incidents produce assurance records; recovery itself must be verified.
capabilities.why: Failure-first law operationalized: failures are governed objects.
dependsOn: Execution lifecycle controls (cancellation, timeouts, retry, idempotency, checkpoints, rollback, recovery, quarantine, escalation)
capabilities.v1Justification: Failure tests mandated (AGENTS.md §31); recovery verification invariant 30.

capabilities.name: Ecosystem model (human, developer, domain, intelligence, infrastructure, integration, partner, application, extension, governance ecosystems)
capabilities.what: Ecosystem ontology: participants, relationships, lifecycle, versioning, dependency graph, interoperability, trust, risk, observability, events across all ecosystem classes.
capabilities.why: CoreGrid is an institutional operating system whose participants and integrations are governed objects.
capabilities.v1Justification: Ecosystem ontology is prescribed, but a minimal V1 may need only identity + integration + marketplace subset; full ecosystem graph breadth is not marked V1-minimum in the corpus.

capabilities.name: Marketplace (controlled exchange)
capabilities.what: Controlled exchange of applications, domain runtimes, extensions, agents, models, tools, datasets, simulations, knowledge packages, APIs, services, compute, capabilities, expertise; every artifact requires identity, publisher provenance, capability declaration, permissions, security assessment, compatibility, version, dependency declaration, integrity verification; marketplace subordinate to governance/security/architecture.
capabilities.why: Extensibility without trust erosion: 'Marketplace participation does not automatically imply trust.'
dependsOn: Ecosystem model (human, developer, domain, intelligence, infrastructure, integration, partner, application, extension, governance ecosystems)
Supply-chain security (part of AI runtime defenses)
capabilities.v1Justification: Marketplace is a growth surface; V1 functions as a platform without third-party exchange. Prescribed in corpus but not required for the loop to close.

capabilities.name: Economic system & resource flows
capabilities.what: Economic system for the platform (billing, value exchange) and resource-flow accounting across ecosystems; workforce economics attribution.
capabilities.why: Institutional operation requires economic controls and attribution.
dependsOn: Ecosystem model (human, developer, domain, intelligence, infrastructure, integration, partner, application, extension, governance ecosystems)
capabilities.v1Justification: Payment security and cost tracking are mandated (AGENTS.md §20/§36); a production platform must account for consumption.

capabilities.name: Ecosystem capability market & extensibility law
capabilities.what: Capability market mechanics and the ecosystem extensibility law (extensions without architectural corruption).
capabilities.why: Extension surfaces must preserve governance.
capabilities.v1Justification: Depends on marketplace; V2 expansion surface.

capabilities.name: Canonical/structured/runtime separation law
capabilities.what: Canonical (mother documents) vs structured (/registry machine-readable) vs runtime (adapters/services) vs evidence vs temporary separation, with promotion rules from temporary to canonical/structured.
capabilities.why: Prevents mission-specific artifacts from silently becoming authoritative.
capabilities.v1Justification: The V1 reconstruction itself relies on this law; it is the anti-drift mechanism for documentation and state.

capabilities.name: Ecosystem observation→action loop
capabilities.what: Ecosystem-level observation → evaluation → action loop with health, drift, debt, failure modes and evolution-without-corruption constraints.
capabilities.why: The platform observes and acts on its own ecosystem state.
capabilities.v1Justification: Ecosystem-level loop is prescribed; minimal V1 needs the runtime-level loop first; ecosystem breadth unmarked.

capabilities.name: Human experience & ecosystem participation
capabilities.what: Human ecosystem: participants, roles, trust, participation models across the platform experience.
capabilities.why: Experience surfaces exist for humans as ecosystem participants.
capabilities.v1Justification: Minimal human participation (authenticated users acting through universal roles) is required for any V1 UI; full experience-design breadth is V2.

capabilities.name: Knowledge graph (relationships with provenance, ownership, authorization, confidence)
capabilities.what: Knowledge graph over people, organizations, schools, devices, buildings, events, resources, workflows, systems; every relationship preserves provenance, ownership, authorization, confidence.
capabilities.why: Relationships must be governed objects, not implicit foreign keys.
capabilities.v1Justification: Relationship identity and confidence are prescribed primitives; the graph is the relationship substrate of the reality model.

capabilities.name: Realtime data governance
capabilities.what: Realtime subscriptions respect tenant, authorization, and privacy; no unauthorized event broadcast.
capabilities.why: Realtime is a surface where tenant isolation is most easily violated.
capabilities.v1Justification: Security invariant; any V1 with live updates needs it.

capabilities.name: Payment security
capabilities.what: Signature validation, idempotency, audit, ownership validation, replay protection; never trust frontend payment state.
capabilities.why: Economic system integrity depends on payment invariants.
dependsOn: Execution lifecycle controls (cancellation, timeouts, retry, idempotency, checkpoints, rollback, recovery, quarantine, escalation)
capabilities.v1Justification: Invariants are prescribed, but the corpus does not mark payments as required for the V1 minimum platform (economic system is prescribed; payment flows may be deferred with billing).

capabilities.name: Frontend security rule (UI is not security)
capabilities.what: Backend enforcement is mandatory; hidden buttons/routes/frontend checks are never the security layer.
capabilities.why: Prevents client-side authorization illusions.
capabilities.v1Justification: Binding architectural rule for all V1 surfaces.

capabilities.name: Secrets governance
capabilities.what: Never commit API keys/passwords/private keys/credentials/service keys; runtime secret security with isolation; secrets as a persisted data category.
capabilities.why: Secret hygiene is a hard security invariant.
dependsOn: Security & trust runtime (identity, capability security, least privilege, domain/environment isolation, secrets)
capabilities.v1Justification: Non-negotiable for V1.

capabilities.name: Assurance auditability & coverage
capabilities.what: Assurance itself must be auditable; assurance coverage measured; assurance gaps explicit; domain-agnostic assurance boundary ('Domain-specific assurance must not become universal architecture').
capabilities.why: The assurance system is itself subject to evidence and conformance.
capabilities.v1Justification: Meta-assurance prevents the assurance layer from becoming an unaccountable authority.

capabilities.name: Multi-actor reality (power, authority, norms, obligations, rights as reality)
capabilities.what: Power and authority, norms and rules, obligations, rights and permissions, responsibility modeled as reality objects; multi-actor reality with competing objectives, cooperation, trust, resource competition, conflict.
capabilities.why: Institutional realities are multi-actor; authorization semantics must be representable IN reality, not only in policy engines.
capabilities.v1Justification: Universal roles and authority modeling depend on representing authority as a reality primitive; domain-neutral and loop-relevant (Decision stage).

capabilities.name: Failure, resilience, recovery & transformation as reality
capabilities.what: Failure as reality, cascades, resilience, recovery, reality transformation and conservation modeled as reality-level phenomena.
capabilities.why: The platform represents real-world failure/recovery, not only system failure.
capabilities.v1Justification: Prescribed ontology; deep reality modeling of cascades/resilience is not marked as V1-minimum, though failure-as-object for the platform itself is (E-102).

capabilities.name: Experiments & experimental evidence
capabilities.what: Experiments as governed reality operations producing experimental evidence with provenance.
capabilities.why: Hypothesis testing requires experiment objects.
capabilities.v1Justification: Prescribed; not marked V1-minimum. Related to adversarial verification but broader.

capabilities.name: Emergence, network reality, influence
capabilities.what: Emergence and collective behavior, network reality, influence modeling.
capabilities.why: Multi-actor and system-dynamics phenomena require emergence/network primitives.
dependsOn: Multi-actor reality (power, authority, norms, obligations, rights as reality)
capabilities.v1Justification: Prescribed ontology; complexity modeling beyond V1 minimum; no source V1 marker.

capabilities.name: Reality state space & trajectories
capabilities.what: Reality state space, trajectory modeling, trajectory divergence analysis.
capabilities.why: Possible futures and scenario comparison require trajectory primitives.
capabilities.v1Justification: Prescribed; depends on simulation; no V1 marker in source.

capabilities.name: Foundry Runtime & AI Engineering Workforce Runtime
capabilities.what: Specialized runtimes for building CoreGrid (Foundry) and for the AI engineering workforce, as first-class runtime components with their own invariants.
capabilities.why: The platform builds itself; the builders need runtime authority boundaries too.
capabilities.v1Justification: Declared as internal components O/P of the runtime topology; status NOT IMPLEMENTED; not explicitly marked V1-minimum, but the loop 'Delegation → Worker Execution' implies an engineering workforce runtime exists in some form.

capabilities.name: Runtime self-description, self-observation, self-repair/evolution boundaries
capabilities.what: Runtime describes and observes itself; self-repair and self-evolution are bounded (never self-authorizing); the self-questioning law requires assurance to be able to disprove the system's own assumptions.
capabilities.why: Autonomy without self-authorization: the platform can improve only through governed evolution.
capabilities.v1Justification: The boundary law (not the capability to auto-evolve) is required in V1: autonomy cannot self-expand (RUNTIME invariant 21).

capabilities.name: Closed architectural loop (three-mother loop)
capabilities.what: IMPLEMENTATION (how built) + RUNTIME (how behaves) + ASSURANCE (how known) forming a closed loop: build → run → verify → drift → evolve → rebuild, with the FINAL COREGRID CONTROL LOOP tying reality, observation, evidence, verification, conformance, progress, drift, evolution.
capabilities.why: The CTO V1 completeness loop is the product-level expression of this closed architectural loop.
capabilities.v1Justification: The loop must close for V1 completeness to be claimable; this is the meta-capability binding all others.

capabilities.name: Domain quarantine (e.g. African Educational Runtime boundary)
capabilities.what: Domain runtimes (e.g. the African Educational Runtime) are quarantined behind explicit boundaries — domain semantics never leak into the universal substrate; education is 'a domain runtime, never the universal ontology'.
capabilities.why: Domain-neutrality enforcement at the surface level; the quarantine boundary is defined in governance.
capabilities.v1Justification: The quarantine boundary must exist in V1 wherever any domain runtime exists.

contradictions.conflict: Canonical mother-surface count is inconsistent: GOVERNANCE.md §50 / COREGRID.md §30 / ENGINEERING.md §3.5 / ARCHITECTURE.md source-of-truth map declare ten canonical mothers, while IMPLEMENTATION.md, RUNTIME.md and ASSURANCE.md each self-declare a 'three-mother architecture' (How built / How behaves / How known) making 12-13 surfaces; GOVERNANCE.md §50 simultaneously forbids creating permanent governance documents, yet PRINCIPLES.md, BOUNDARIES.md, DEPENDENCY.md, CONSTITUTION.md, DECISIONS.md, REGISTRY.md exist as permanent root governance artifacts.

PROGRESS.md §01 declares a different document-authority list ('1. CONSTITUTION.md, 2. ARCHITECTURE-PRINCIPLES.md, 3. ARCHITECTURE-REGISTRY.md, 4. ARCHITECTURE-DEPENDENCY-MAP.md, 5. ARCHITECTURE-BOUNDARIES.md, 6. ARCHITECTURE-POLICIES.md, 7. ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md, 8. individual phase specs, 9. approved contracts') that directly contradicts GOVERNANCE.md §50's ten-mother canon and its prohibition of permanent governance documents.

Authority ladders disagree: GOVERNANCE.md §4 has Levels 0-9 (Identity → Governance → Architecture → Reality Model → Engineering → Workforce → Missions → Blueprints → Progress → Ecosystem, no CONSTITUTION); PRINCIPLES.md/BOUNDARIES.md use CONSTITUTION → ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES → ARCHITECTURE → REGISTRY → DEPENDENCIES → BOUNDARIES → PHASE SPECIFICATIONS (includes CONSTITUTION, omits WORKFORCE/PROGRESS/ECOSYSTEM); CONSTITUTION.md claims constitutional supremacy; CP-01 uses CONSTITUTION → GOVERNANCE → ARCHITECTURE → REALITY → ENGINEERING → PHASE/MISSION/BLUEPRINT → SCHEMA → REGISTRY → STATE/EVIDENCE/EXECUTION.

Generation-marker conflict: PRINCIPLES.md self-declares 'Architecture Generation: CoreGrid V3 / Civilization Architecture', REGISTRY.md 'Architecture Version: v4.0', CONSTITUTION.md 'Architecture Era: CoreGrid ASI-Era', DECISIONS.md scopes 'Phase 01–Phase 51', and PRINCIPLES/BOUNDARIES/DEPENDENCY/CONSTITUTION/DECISIONS/REGISTRY banners speak of V2/V3 FROZEN buckets — while the CTO RULING-8 brief permits only V1/V2 buckets and forbids V3+ buckets. The six governance artifacts carry an older bucket model than the ruling.

Duplicate-authority conflict: IMPLEMENTATION.md §6.4 ownership matrix assigns 'CoreGrid identity → Architecture / Registry' (dual owner), while ARCHITECTURE.md's source-of-truth map assigns 'CoreGrid identity → COREGRID.md' and REGISTRY.md §0 claims the registry is the canonical architectural index — three different owners for platform identity.

REALITY.md §149 correctly separates universal from domain semantics, yet earlier sections (§5 entity examples School/Student/Teacher/Mine/Mineral Deposit, §10 state examples 'School = Open, Student = Enrolled, Mine = Operational', §16 relationship semantics TEACHES/STUDIES/EMPLOYS, §24 process examples Education/Mining/Disease Progression, §27 activities Teach/Mine/Diagnose) present domain vocabulary inside the universal-ontology surface without quarantine markers.

Consistent in principle (simulation/prediction must never silently become direct observation) but stated as an evidence-class rule in ASSURANCE and as a runtime invariant in RUNTIME with different enumeration granularity (7 evidence classes vs 40 flat invariants) — a harmonization burden, not a logical conflict.
The V5 addendum appears twice verbatim in COREGRID.md (~lines 1310-1520 and ~1534-1744) including the 12 control-plane mechanism list — an editorial duplication that risks divergent future edits.

CONTROL-PLANE.md master surface says mission orchestration / durable execution records are 'designed but not established as a product runtime' while CP-06/07/08 self-declare 'NOT ESTABLISHED / NOT IMPLEMENTED' — consistent, but CP-08 is titled 'CURSOR EXECUTION' while its §1 defines a general 'Execution System'; CONTROL-PLANE.md explicitly downgrades Cursor execution to 'an engineering-tool boundary, not a CoreGrid runtime authority' — the CP-08 file title overstates it.

DECISIONS.md header says 'Document: DECISION.md' (singular, mismatched filename DECISIONS.md) and phase scope 'Phase 01–Phase 51'; REGISTRY.md declares 'Registered Architecture Phase Capacity: 51' and 'Civilization Architecture Layers: 7'; DEPENDENCY.md says '51 Registered Phases' — but architecture/ contains phase-01 through phase-52 directories/files (phase-52 exists), so the registered phase count is inconsistent with the phase corpus.
